text_fidelity_a: EXPLORATION GADGET Ferro Rod Fire Starter I had such hopes for this based on the 5 star "even kids can do it!" reviews present when I got this, but there must be a trick I don't know about. I tried to light a pile of brush (dry leaves, small twigs, small branches, and some newspaper stuck in several spots). Holding the rod about an inch above the crumpled newspaper, I scraped the rod with the raised edge of the ruler/striker gadget. After scraping off the black coating, I could get a shower of sparks with each scrape, but nothing caught fire. After about 50 scrapes, only one spark even smoldered a second. I tried over dry kindling, the twigs and leaves, but nothing caught fire. Even if I got a fire to start in a little bowl (like one reviewer did in demonstration; thank you!), you'd still need a spill (long bit of twisted paper or something like match wood) to get the flame started on several spots on the brush pile. So it's a no-go as a fire-starter in practical situations. I was able to start the fire later with only one match, BTW.

text_fidelity_a:
Contigo Superior 2.0 Stainless Steel Travel Mug with Handle and Leak-Proof Lid, Double-Wall Insulation Keeps Drinks Hot up to 7 Hours or Cold up to 18 Hours, 20oz Juniper When I order a product I am more interested in the negative reviews than the positive ones. What problems are other people having? Do the buyers understand how the product works or are they misusing it? Are there design errors in the product? Does it function as advertised? Is it possible that a string of bad reviews is due to a switch in manufacturers? That by the way is often the case and a company has to own that choice.

My first use resulted in an unintended torture test. After filling up the mug with my first cup of coffee in the morning -- when I am still a bit fumble fingered -- I dropped the full mug on our marble floor. You know that moment when the dropped item appears suspended in the air and you are anticipating a horrible crash and the resulting mess? Didn't happen here! Boy was I relieved. I hate to catch flak from my wife to start the day.

Since my wife will be using this mug on her commute to work I was most interested in the claim that it would keep liquids "hot for up to 7 hours". So I filled it up with hot coffee at 10:00 pm and opened it this morning at 7:00 am. For the mathematically challenged, which most of the younger kids seem to be these days, that is nine hours. When I popped the lid one-handed (which takes a bit of practice) and took a sip, I was rewarded with coffee that was better than warm but not quite hot.

Most users of course will not use this as a thermos to keep something hot or cold for 8-10 hours. Instead they will be steadily drinking/sipping from the cup until the beverage is finished. Constant repetitive opening and closing of the tab is bound to release heat faster and the remaining liquid will no doubt be at less than a desired temperature, but it was nice to see that it would function as promised.

So Contigo got it's act together, either by changing something in the product or finding a better manufacturer. The mug is a subtle pleasing color and fits perfectly in our vehicles. The lid opening mechanism comes stiff and takes a bit of use to work it loose. Even though the company says that you can put the lid (only) in the dishwasher, I always get better long-term results by hand washing them. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Contigo Superior 2.0 Stainless Steel Travel Mug with Handle and Leak-Proof Lid, Double-Wall Insulation Keeps Drinks Hot up to 7 Hours or Cold up to 18 Hours, 20oz Juniper

text_fidelity_a:
EXERPEUTIC EXERWORK 2000i Bluetooth Folding Exercise Desk Bike with 24 Workout Programs and Free App Ordered in October and it is now February. 4 months of use. Sort of.
The exercise-work-bike took a total of 3 days to put together, and had I been doing it alone, I probably never would have gotten it. There is some form of blue “insta-glue” on the pedal screws that made them nearly impossible to screw in. 3 neighborhood kids and teenagers tried their best to help a lady out, but to no avail. Eventually, I hung my head in shame and begged the assistance of male-friend to demonstrate his masculinity and wield tools to get the pedal screwed in.
I am 5’8. That’s 68 inches or about 172cm.
The next issue came when I realized that even at the lowest adjustment, the one recommended for 5’1-5’4 heights, I still struggled to reach the pedals, sitting with my back comfortably against the backrest. If I scooched forward just enough that half my cheeks were off the front of the seat I could reach the pedals, the backrest, and still use the desk for my laptop! But the desk was still a bit high, so I used the tilt-a-table adjustment to relax my wrists and type with perfectly non-ergonomical T-Rex arms.
And now the clunking noise. I can’t stand it. It started off quiet, but after maybe 100 miles of use, it makes a clunking noise from the pedals and no matter how many times I tighten the bolts (almost to stripping them), the seat keeps wobbling and the handle bars offer very little support.

Overall, as a workout bike, it give options that a regular bike doesn’t have—a table.
As for the rest, I am very unhappy with the very little use I got out of it, the lack of structural support for a solid working/workout of cycling, and how fast it has started having issues.
text_fidelity_b: EXERPEUTIC EXERWORK 2000i Bluetooth Folding Exercise Desk Bike with 24 Workout Programs and Free App

JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion Pickleball Paddle - Carbon Surface with High Grit & Spin, Elongated Handle, USAPA Approved 2022 Ben Johns Paddle - Available with Pickle Ball Paddle Cover My wife and I are pretty much beginner players, having only played in high school (a long while back) and coming into the sport anew. So please take that into consideration in this review.

We each got a JOOLA paddle, slightly different, and like them both. We know nothing about the brand, we are not experts on what brands or elements of a paddle are best, but we are trying different ones. This JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion Pickleball Paddle so far is very nice and I do like it. Mine is slightly heavier than hers, and I do notice the difference in weight, and as negligible as the difference really is, it is noticeable. We're actually surprised by how such a little amount can be felt. That said, I do not have an issue when swinging or hitting due to the "added weight." It feels like a smooth swing, a solid contact.

I think what I like most is the grip. I can FEEL the solid connection with the handle. From the moment we each first held ours, the number one thing we felt and noticed and were drawn to in each of our JOOLA paddles is the GRIP. This alone is likely going to make my JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion Pickleball Paddle my go-to paddle. As we get better, it might change, but right now, I like that connection to the paddle.

In the end, I like this JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion Pickleball Paddle and am very happy to have it.
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Ben Johns Hyperion Pickleball Paddle - Carbon Surface with High Grit & Spin, Elongated Handle, USAPA Approved 2022 Ben Johns Paddle - Available with Pickle Ball Paddle Cover

As such, I always wished someone made nicer heat-reflecting blankets, still at an affordable price - and Adventure Medical Kits delivers.  Each blanket is large enough to make a decent shelter, beef up a tent or makeshift shelter, or for two people to wrap themselves in. I have one blanket I've used dozens of times, and it's only just starting to show some wear here and there.  For the price, I definitely got my money's worth, many times over.  I recommend everyone have one or more in their car or home, in case of emergency.  For anyone involved in outdoor sports, these are phenomenal.  It's another great product from Adventure Medical Kits!

text_fidelity_a:
Energizer LED Camping Lantern, 240-400 High Lumens, IPX4 Water Resistant, Battery Powered LED, Use For Camping, Hiking, Emergency Light, Batteries Included I got this LED lantern to use as an emergency light and for when we need an area flashlight at night on our farm. It's worked well for this purpose. I no longer camp, but my first thought on testing this lantern was that I wished I'd had something like this back in my camping days. It's very bright compared to other lantern flashlights I've had in the past, but you can dim the light to about half strength using the dimmer button. You can use the lantern as a directional light or extend the light up above the base to make it an area light. There's a stand that can be pulled out from the back of the base so you can put the lantern on a table or floor. The orange grip is lightly textured and rubber-like for a secure hold when carrying it.

When you rotate the light upward, the white plastic back reflector is exposed. This is how you access the battery area. There are two flat-screw-head type locks that need to be rotated clockwise by a quarter turn to access the batteries. I actually opened them using the back of a clothespin. lol. The lantern comes with 4 batteries, but it can take 8 AA batteries--for longer life, I assume, but I've not tried it.

The on-off button is on the back of the base. You push the button to turn the light on or off, or you hold it to dim the light and release the button when the light is at the desired level. At first, I occasionally had trouble with not removing my finger quickly enough from the button and getting a dim instead of turning the light off. I just needed to learn to "jab" the button rather than taking my time. The lantern looks fairly durable and easy to clean, but I've only given it light use so far.

The instruction manual is pretty brief, but it does cover all the "how to use" information. Instructions you might wish to know now: "To disable Try Me mode, remove batteries from compartment and wait 10 seconds. Reinsert batteries and wait 10 seconds before pressing switch." and "Lantern is water resistant and suitable for use outside. Do not submerse or attempt to operate under water."

According to the packaging, the light was made in China and the batteries were made in Singapore.
text_fidelity_b: Energizer LED Camping Lantern, 240-400 High Lumens, IPX4 Water Resistant, Battery Powered LED, Use For Camping, Hiking, Emergency Light, Batteries Included

I'm able to work out all of my major muscle groups with this, and get a really full workout using this. I usually use only one or two bands, depending on the exercise, because the full 120 lbs of resistance with all 3 bands is usually too much for my workouts.

It's also light enough and compact enough that I can throw it in my suitcase when I travel. It's also way better than all the equipment in most hotel gyms. The bands are 5 feet long, and they stretch a lot, so even if you're really weak, then you can get a good workout with these, and not get frustrated.

At first, I was going to throw away the closed door attachment, and I'm super glad that I didn't. It's awesome! You put it on any door, and then it uses the strength of the frame and the hinges and the closed door for resistance. It's like you've attached the bands to a cement wall. It doesn't leave marks on the door, and works amazingly well.

The only bad thing is that it looks like it's out of stock, and may have been discontinued. You can still get the parts and piece this together, though.

My biggest complaint is the leg rest where you sit when operating this machine. it has four foam pads to aid in comfort, but the plate between them is solid metal and should also have a foam cap. text_fidelity_a:
Covacure Beach Towels Lightweight Travel Towel Set, Quick Dry Towel (63"x32") & Carrying Bag for Beach, Travel, Swim, Pool, Camping, Outdoors and Sports Towel This a handy towel for mobile adventures. It isn't as fluffy and snuggly as a thick cotton bath towel, but it's really absorbent, dries quicker, and rolls up into a much smaller bundle, making it a great alternative for taking along when space is limited.

The towel's compact portability is one of it's strongest features. It comes neatly folded and rolled up in a nylon and mesh drawstring bag. It's a bit of a thrash getting it back into the stuff sack folded up if you don't roll it nice and tight. I find it far easier to just stuff it in like you would a sleeping bag, starting with one corner of the towel and packing it in tight starting at the bottom. The packed bag measures about 8 inches long and 5 inches in diameter, so it takes up lots less room in your duffel bag or backpack than a regular towel. I've attached a photo of the packed towel in my hand to give you an idea of its size.

The towel is just over 5 feet long and not quite 3 feet wide. If you use it to lay on at the beach, your feet will end up in the sand, and not on the towel, unless you're under 5 feet tall.

The microfiber fabric is quite absorbent, easily drying me completely after a shower.

It also dries faster than my normal cotton bath towel. There's an elastic loop crudely sewn onto one corner of the towel to hang it by (see attached photo). I don't usually use the loop because you need a pretty high hook to keep the towel off the ground when you hang it by the loop. Instead, I just hang it by the middle across a peg or hook to dry.

The biggest drawback I've noticed is the feel of the towel aganst my skin. Instead of the soft, snuggly fluff of a regular bath or beach towel, this towel feels more like a sheet of suede or chamois leather. For that reason, it won't replace my bath towel at home, but I do think that it's a reasonable compromise for an efficient travel accessory. It seems particularly useful for carrying to the beach or pool, and for camping or adventure travel (staying in hostels, for example) where you'll need to provide your own towel.
If that's the kind of stuff you do, this towel should work well for you.

Let me know if you found anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Covacure Beach Towels Lightweight Travel Towel Set, Quick Dry Towel (63"x32") & Carrying Bag for Beach, Travel, Swim, Pool, Camping, Outdoors and Sports Towel

text_fidelity_a:
Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow Good anti stress eye pillow. What I like about the Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy pillow
1) I like the fragrance of the lavender and chamomile pillow.
2) The fragrance is not overwhelming it is subtle.
3) It is not overstuffed so it drapes nicely over your eye and sinus area when you are lying flat.
4) The silk has a cooling effect
5) I have chronic sinusitis and this pillow feels like it helps to relieve some of that tight pressure pain. It also seems to calm the area around my eyes.
I have used several different sinus pillow type remedies over the years for that "ahhh relief!" moment when you can feel the swelling and ache diminishing.Not many were very effective but this one and the Lavender eye pillow by AyaZen are both effective. However, I would choose the one from AyaZen over this one because:
1) It can be heated and froze as long as you put it in a plastic sealed bag so it doesn't absorb freezer odor.
2) It has more filling and a more balanced filling making it a little weightier than the Earth Therapeutics eye pillow
3) The velvet like cover of the AyaZen is soft and luxurious yet it also has a griping effect so it doesn't readily slip off your face.
4) It has a stronger lavender scent that is soothing but not overwhelming.
5) For me, this pillow relieves the pain and pressure associated with my sinusitis better.

As a comparison, they are both good eye pillows but AyaZen wins for me.

The reason Earth Therapeutics is not a perfect five stars and doesn't win for me:
1) It doesn't have the balanced filling the AyaZen does
2) The silk used to encase the Earth Therapeutics pillow slips very easily unless you are lying down flat.If your head happens to turn a little while sleeping at an angle or with your head raised at any height, it slips off. Even though you can conform it to your eyes and nose it won't stay because of the silkiness of the material and the almost whisper light weight of the pillow. If your head is raised at any angle or your head happens to fall sideways while napping, you must continually reposition the pillow.
3) you cannot heat it in the microwave or put it in the freezer. I know this pillow is suppose to be Therapeutic based solely on the oils it harbors and the silk that encases it but it just needs a little more to really reach that Therapeutic level.

I bought this based on it conforming to the face and being Therapeutic. However, I often sleep with my head raised up or in my recliner because of breathing issues due to my sinuses.The silk of this pillow would always cause it to slip down or sideways causing me to wake up and recenter it on my eyes. Overall, I would recommend this pillow for someone who doesn't have to sleep with the head or upper body raised at any height and doesn't have to turn their head much while napping. The silk does have a cooling effect and the lavender and chamomile does help to relieve some of the pressure and pain.
text_fidelity_b: Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow

Splatterburst Targets - 12 x12 inch (5) Bullseye Reactive Shooting Target - Shots Burst Bright Fluorescent Yellow Upon Impact - Gun - Rifle - Pistol - Airsoft - BB Gun - Air Rifle I use these splatter targets whenever I have to sight in a new .22 rifle. Each rifle I buy has a threaded barrel so that I can attach an AAC suppressor and do the shooting in my backyard. Using a 4X scope or higher allows you to easily keep track of your hits without having to rely on another person or a spotting scope. Since no one has a clue as to what I'm doing, I can take the time to do a good job with each rig.

First off I use a boresighter on the larger center target to zero each gun in properly. When I'm satisfied with my efforts, I'll then use three bullets from a different manufacturer--or a different configuration from the same manufacturer--on each of the four smaller targets to determine which ammo each gun likes best. I usually have about eight different types of ammo on hand so it takes two of these splatter targets to get the job done.

When I put each gun back in the rack, I tape the bottom of each stock with the name of the ammo that seems to work best in that gun/scope combination. After a few days I'll take the newly sighted in guns back outside to try the different types of ammo once more--just to be sure. Since I'm able to do this in my own backyard it saves me a lot of time driving to/from the range and waiting out the other shooters to change targets. I've also used this method to break in some suppressed .22 pistols.

Great targets, easy to use and easy to see.
text_fidelity_b: Splatterburst Targets - 12 x12 inch (5) Bullseye Reactive Shooting Target - Shots Burst Bright Fluorescent Yellow Upon Impact - Gun - Rifle - Pistol - Airsoft - BB Gun - Air Rifle

Said stove which still works at this junction is less than 15 feet as the crow flies from the EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove which I set up beside the BBQ grill so as to have a place to set stuff.

We cooked hamburgers, hash brown and pork and beans on the thing awhile ago on a cast iron skillet. Good gracious! I mean a mere piddly handful of twigs cooked the whole meal! It's insane, really. Tell you what...when these things first got popular about 10 years ago I took a look, called it nonsense and never looked back. And then, well, things changed. Our EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove is rightfully the backup for the backup. A real 'just in case' thing. However, were I in it just for fun I could prolly think up a dozen reasons to have one for outdoor fun. But I'm not funning here. I'm very serious. Times are serious.

Not being a metal worker or a brick layer I turned to this device which in all of its simplicity has struck just the right note. It is a little smoky to start, but as it heats up there is very little, just like everyone says. It cooks pretty hot to begin, but by jiggling the sticks we got pretty decent heat control. Smaller sticks for a burst of hot, etc. The next morning I wiped off the outside and spritzed the top and grate with a little spray olive oil as a protectant. I'd estimate that one 5 gal bucket of yard sticks will yield 4-5 complete meals such as I described above.

I'm as pleased as punch, and not a little amazed. What pushed me over was a couple of vids done by EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove's biggest fan in England on YT. In answer to my question he advised that he's had his for over 6 years and uses it regularly. Simple, light weight, and it lasts. If you're circling like I did, go ahead and land on it. You'll be thankin' me. Guaranteed.

Lastly a pro tip. If you are unaccustomed to cooking over wood just be advised to scrub the outside and bottom of your cookware as well as you do the inside. It will get smoky.
text_fidelity_b: EcoZoom Versa, High-Efficiency, Wood-Burning, 14.25 lbs Portable Rocket Stove for Outdoor Cooking

First off a presta valve is the stupidest thing ever and they suck, I will definitely be replacing them on my new bike soon. A standard tire valve is 100% easier and more reliable, no idea why these even exist?  That being said this pump totally failed to make solid connect with the presta valve. I just ended up loosing all the air from my tire. The problem is that the pump using its tube connector just did not make a clean connection to the bike's presta valve. When it seemingly DID make a connection  there was no air flow because it had closed the tip of the presta valve. I finally gave up and used my regular bicycle pump and inflated my tire with ease. I have a high end Trek bike with a high quality valve. The pump is pretty nice otherwise and I assume the standard/non-presta connector pump works OK but did not try it.

HOPSOOKEN 30L Ultra Lightweight Travel Water Resistant Packable Backpack for Hiking Cycling Sports Daypack Backpack/Ultralight and Handy (Black New) This is a lightweight (in all aspects) bag that is great for limited purposes. It is made out of extremely thin and flexible material. It can fold up into itself and zip up (see picture) for easy storage and transport when not using it to carry items in. I can see this bag as being an excellent option for travelers who might find themselves needing another bag/storage option at the last minute. Like when you realize at the airport your bag is overweight and to avoid a huge baggage fee, you wish you had a small bag you could put some heavy items in and carry it on the plane instead. This would be perfect for that. Or you spend the holidays with relatives and they send you home with more goodies for the kids than you have room in your luggage for.

It's not a primary use bag. There is no padding at all. Not in the bottom of the bag. Not in the shoulder straps. There is no protection for items within the bag or your shoulders. It would not be comfortable carrying this with anything substantial or heavy inside. The material reminds me of an inexpensive windbreaker or poncho.

Pros:
Great backup bag for unexpected situations
Lightweight and very compact
Folds and zips into itself for easy storage and transport

Cons:
Flimsy shoulder straps with no padding
Questionable ability to carry heavy, rigid items like books or glass bottles
No padding in the bag itself, thus no protection for items inside

I received this bag for minimal cost in exchange for my unbiased review.
text_fidelity_b: HOPSOOKEN 30L Ultra Lightweight Travel Water Resistant Packable Backpack for Hiking Cycling Sports Daypack Backpack/Ultralight and Handy (Black New)

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ325 Alvita Ultimate Pedometer, Blue I do a lot of walking. A little over a year ago, I was diagnosed as being diabetic (type 2). I've been able to manage it by modifying my diet and daily exercise. I've been walking for at least 30 minutes every day, some days for an hour. Walking really brings down my blood sugar after eating. So I was happy to get one of these Omron pedometers to try out for a month.

Setting up the meter was pretty simple. You just had to install the battery and set the meter. Setting the meter entailed setting the time and putting in your stride length. To find your stride length you simply walk normally for ten steps - measure the distance (in inches), the divide by 10 (mine was 26 inches). There are some other settings - for example using km vs miles. Sounds more complicated than it is. Just be sure to read the instructions.

The meter comes with a few accessories such as a silicone case, a clip, and lanyard. The silicone case has a clip on the back of it, so that is what I used. I clipped the meter to the pocket-watch pocket on my blue-jeans. Which worked great, till I went out walking after lunch and came back without the meter. I'm guessing at some point the pedometer popped off and fell to the ground while I was walking. When I discovered it missing I retraced my steps and tried to find it - unsuccessfully. One of my co-workers even went out and tried to find it. Most of the path I walk in the after-noon is public sidewalks and tend to be heavily used by other walkers - so I'm guessing someone found it. I had the pedometer for about a week before losing it.

IMO -it was my own fault. I was wearing headphones at the time listening to an audiobook. And in hindsight, I should have attached the lanyard strap to the clip and hooked that to a belt-loop. I really suggest doing that.

The pedometer worked fine for me. I compared it to another meter and got similar readings. Operating the meter was easy - there are just three buttons. I really wish I hadn't lost mine.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ325 Alvita Ultimate Pedometer, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Soozier Adjustable Seated Calf Raise Machine Leg Press Machine Strength Training Gym Equipment This calf raise machine is a great value piece of equipment for any home gym, on a budget. It's fairly comfortable, and allows you to easily do seated calf raises, and standing if you want to improvise a little bit. The big selling point is price, since many weight loaded seated calf machines are much more expensive for such a relatively simple movement. A big upside is there is pretty decent options for size adjustment to fit most people's needs.

The downsides are probably what allow the cost to be so low. While QC isn't necessarily bad, many pieces are not 'tight fitting', and need additional washers/spacers to make for a snug fit. Some pieces also needed to be manually widened so others would fit. Mechanically, this is a simplified seat calf machine, and takes several shortcuts in design that hurt QOL, such as the seat is mounted on the fulcrum, so you move as you perform the calf raise, and the handle to mount/unmount the machine from rest is on the rest-bar itself, in front of your knees, making it a little awkward to get in/out of. These are not deal breakers, but if you're used to 'gym-quality' equipment, this is does not meet the standard. However! it's so cheap that it doesn't even matter. Still get nasty calf pumps with this machine, 10/10 would buy again, as long as the price is cheap ~150$.
text_fidelity_b: Soozier Adjustable Seated Calf Raise Machine Leg Press Machine Strength Training Gym Equipment

text_fidelity_a:
Folding Stool with Storage Bag, Lightweight Outdoor Chair Aluminum Alloy Bracket Camping Stool for Fishing, Hiking, Camping, Traveling and BBQ (Silver) I”ll be honest, I did not get this Folding Stool with Storage Bag as a sitting stool but for my feet. We have a new chair from here on Amazon, that is a bit tall for my shorter legs and while the chair is comfortable, I knew that over longer periods of time it will start to be uncomfortable. I thought if I had a foot stool it would be better. Spotted this Folding Stool with Storage Bag and grabbed it. I was right - it goes perfectly with the chair. But it also will make a good additional sitting spot if needed. Or could hold some lighter things - well balanced if we’re careful. The Folding Stool with Storage Bag comes in that storage bag - pull it out and as you’re kind of moving it around, it starts to put itself into those legs. Meaning the legs go together very easily. They are like a lot of newer things - they are connected by a line that keeps them ‘together’ then push them into one another and they stay in place. I don’t know that I’m explaining it well, but it’s easy. Watch so the seat goes the correct way - if not, you’ll pull it open a little and flip it the right way - no worries. And you’re good. I’m a heavier guy right now. I sat on it, but didn’t really put my full weight on it - and for me it was only sort of comfortable at this weight. My wife is lighter, but she too was so-so on sitting comfort. I think a smaller person or child would do best. It was fairly sturdy for the weight - but I would not last too long on it and she didn’t think she would either. But using it to prop my legs across was just fine. Felt good, was comfortable, and I am pretty sure it’ll be great for that kind of thing.

In the end I gave it 4 rather than 5 stars because of the ability to hold a larger person is not there, and even at a smaller weight, I don’t think it’s wide enough for someone to go very long on. I have not always been my current weight and it is coming off, but even when I get back down, I don’t think it would be comfortable enough to last more than a few minutes without preferring to move to a chair. But, for a foot rest, it’s good. I am glad to have this Folding Stool with Storage Bag, but it will “only” work for limited things.
text_fidelity_b: Folding Stool with Storage Bag, Lightweight Outdoor Chair Aluminum Alloy Bracket Camping Stool for Fishing, Hiking, Camping, Traveling and BBQ (Silver)

Adjusting seat or handlebars. You have to remove the bolt, move what you are adjusting, line the bolt up, and refasten it. If it is only one person using the bike, that is no big deal. If you share it and have to change it regularly it soon gets old.

Coleman White Water Adult Sleeping Bag, Big & Tall Our family does a lot of camping due to the boys and myself being in a scouting organization and enjoying the outdoors. I have been camping since I was a kid and have slept in numerous sleeping bags and have owned numerous coleman sleeping bags. I bought this Coleman White Water Large Cool-Weather Scoop Sleeping Bag from Amazon when it was a lightning deal back in November 2015. I have used the bag solely on our camp-outs since then. I have slept in it over a dozen nights under the stars in different temperature and weather conditions. Majority of the nights have been clear and low humidity with temperatures between 35-65 degrees.

This bag could sleep one and a half people (me and one of my kids) or one large person hence the name “large” in the title. In the description on Amazon says the bag is designed for 30-50 degree weather. We spent one weekend under the stars in the lower to mid 30s and it was cold and needed another blanket, however other nights between 40-60 degrees it is very comfortable.

So I would rate this sleeping bag 40 degrees and above. We do live in Georgia and humidity is high even in the winter time so in another climate 30 degrees may be comfortable in this bag. I liked that it is very comfortable sleeping on the ground with one of the most comfortable interiors of any sleeping bag i have slept in. The sleeping bag is made of 100% Polyester with 100% cotton fill. Overall a great deal if you can find it on sale.

Positives:
+Oversized for comfort
+Zipper does not get stuck in the material
+Comfortable (40-60 degrees)
+Five year warranty on stitching and workmanship

Negatives:
-Is not comfortable low to mid 30s
-Does not come with storage bag
text_fidelity_b: Coleman White Water Adult Sleeping Bag, Big & Tall

text_fidelity_a:
Thule DoubleTrack Pro XT 2 Hitch Bike Rack I have no one to blame but myself for trusting this rack would be suitable.
As others have noted, the single post with two locking hook design makes it very very difficult to mount two same frame height bikes simultaneously. But what's worse is that there's no easy way to load the bikes on the rack! If the locking post is upright, then the hook gets in the way of the bike. If the post is lying flat, then once you've put your bikes on there is no way to raise the post without removing the hooks first. Also, you can't keep the bike standing upright while moving the post, because the tire obstructs the locking hook, so you need to be prepared to have the bike lean on your car trunk. What a design disaster.
Make sure to try the rack before you buy. None of the youtube videos will point out these issues. And those guys showing how they easily get their ebikes on the rack? Good luck with that. You'll need to be in pretty good shape to do that heavy lifting.
text_fidelity_b: Thule DoubleTrack Pro XT 2 Hitch Bike Rack
